10755.description: Displayed wearing the false serial 1901 and earlier 752 per Wrecks and Relics Online. The number 1901 belongs to the MiG-15UTI at the Almaza museum. aviationmuseum.eu reads the marking as 1902.

10756.description: Displayed wearing the false serial 658 per Wrecks and Relics Online. aviationmuseum.eu gives the serial as 5001 which is the photographically confirmed serial of the Almaza MiG-21F-13 so that reading is rejected.

10757.description: Construction number 61144 and civil registration SU-AVE. Wrecks and Relics Online records it displayed "As 42" but photographs taken by the Egypt Wikimedians User Group on 14 February 2026 show it marked 601 so the display marking has been changed since that compilation was written.

10758.description: Displayed wearing the false serial 7751 and earlier 803 per Wrecks and Relics Online. The number 7751 belongs to the Su-17K at the Almaza museum.

10759.description: Wrecks and Relics Online records it displayed "As 46" but a photograph taken by the Egypt Wikimedians User Group on 14 February 2026 shows 151 in Arabic-Indic numerals on the forward fuselage so the marking has been changed. aviationmuseum.eu reports 151 as if it were the serial.

10760.description: True identity not established. Wrecks and Relics Online records it displayed "As 61" while aviationmuseum.eu reports 201; neither is a confirmed serial so tail_number is left blank. Seen and described at this museum by Richard Seaman.

10767.description: Construction number 168-377. Carries a Tunisian civil registration. Recorded by Wrecks and Relics Online from a photograph by R.H. Dijkhuizen in March 2020.

10768.description: Monument at Hurghada. Wrecks and Relics Online last noted it January 2024.

10766.description: Gate guard at Helwan about 2 km east of the aircraft factory display point.

10770.description: Roadside monument in Ismailia mapped by Wrecks and Relics Online from satellite imagery.

10773.description: Mounted nose-high on a pole at a gate in Khartoum. A Wikimedia Commons photograph taken on 9 April 2019 during the sit-in outside the air force command shows a pole-mounted MiG-21 with a three-digit nose number consistent with 344 although the resolution does not permit a certain reading. The identity 344 comes from Wrecks and Relics Online whose record for this point was last updated in April 2013 so survival through the 2023 to 2025 fighting is unverified.

10781.description: Construction number N.6474. Preserved at Meknes air base alongside a MiG-17. Distinct from the several cannibalised F-5 hulks recorded elsewhere on the same field which are not displays.

10782.description: Construction number 1406029 and also carries the code 05. Preserved at Meknes air base. Morocco briefly operated Soviet-supplied MiG-17s in the early 1960s so this is a rare survivor of that period.

10783.description: Construction number N.6226. Preserved at a second Meknes point about 300 m west of the F-5A and MiG-17 pair.

10786.description: Also carries the code 275. The single military aircraft in the museum forecourt alongside a tank a missile and a military truck as described by the French Wikipedia article. A Flickr photograph dated 30 November 2016 shows it in place and its caption states the type served from 1963 to 1981.

10787.description: Royal Moroccan Air Force Mirage F1EH brought down over Western Sahara and exhibited as a war trophy by the Polisario Front at Rabuni in the Sahrawi refugee camps near Tindouf. Recorded by Wrecks and Relics Online as a wreck rather than a complete airframe and refreshed 19 March 2025. A 1996 photograph on the Northrop F-5 Enthusiast Page shows an F-5A and an F-5E at the same museum but neither has been confirmed since.

10692.description: Former Armee de l'Air Mirage F1C-200 preserved on the base wearing code 33-FO. Last noted February 2025.

10789.description: Construction number R.1190. Wrecks and Relics Online last noted the museum group October 2022 and refreshed the site record March 2025.

10790.description: Also carries the code AB. Wrecks and Relics Online last noted it October 2022.

10791.description: Construction number 585812. The Tunisian L-59T is the export Super Albatros. Wrecks and Relics Online last noted it October 2022.

10792.description: Construction number 1263. Wrecks and Relics Online last noted it October 2022.

10793.description: Construction number 2675. Delivered to Air France in 1951 as F-BBDT and transferred to Royal Air Maroc in 1960. Retired from service in 1970 and used as a training airframe at Anfa. Restored and repainted in historic Royal Air Maroc colours in 2004 and 2005. Constellation Survivors records it still parked outside the hangar in October 2022 and Wrecks and Relics Online last noted the group October 2024.

10693.description: French civil-registered Beech 18 recorded as preserved in the Djibouti display group. Unlike the five military airframes at this site it carries no recent last-noted date so its continued presence is the least certain of the group.

10797.description: Construction number 1009. The oldest airframe in the Royal Air Maroc collection.

10798.description: Construction number 4340. Preserved at Rabat-Sale air base. A second Moroccan Do 28D-2 registered CNA-NP is recorded as stored at Ben Slimane rather than displayed and is excluded.

10799.description: Construction number 91-424. Wrecks and Relics Online refreshed this site from satellite imagery on 21 April 2026 which is the most recent currency evidence found for any Tunisian display.

10800.description: Construction number 1795 and also carries the code 3. Refreshed from satellite imagery 21 April 2026. Distinct from Alouette II L51-003 construction number 1811 at the Tunis science museum.

10802.description: Construction number 528919104. Carries a Sudanese civil registration. Present in the 27 December 2025 satellite count.

10803.description: Present in the 27 December 2025 satellite count of four airframes at the museum.

10804.description: Sudan bought the piston-engined Provost T.53 in the late 1950s. Present in the 27 December 2025 satellite count.

10805.description: Construction number 1096. The 376th Bombardment Group B-24D that overflew its base returning from Naples on 4 April 1943 and was found intact in the Libyan Sand Sea in November 1958. The remains were recovered in August 1994 by a team led by Dr Fadel Ali Mohamed and taken to Tobruk. Wrecks and Relics Online places the wreck at a museum in Tobruk city and refreshed the record 19 March 2025 while Wikipedia states it is at Gamal Abdel Nasser air base about 25 km south-west. The discrepancy is unresolved. This is a wreck rather than a restored airframe and pieces have been souvenired over the decades.

10811.description: Supplied to Portugal by France in 1961 and used in the Portuguese Colonial War. The second of the pair displayed in the open plaza of the Fortaleza de Sao Miguel, described as well recovered and maintained. Confirmed present by a visitor account of a March 2025 visit.

37948.description: Also carried CNA-MH; c/n 11283; plinthed at Marrakech; last sighting Oct 2018

10812.description: Construction number CBAF.44. Entered Southern Rhodesian Air Force service as SR65 on 28 March 1951; struck off charge 1954 and redesignated RRAF65 in October 1954. Subsequently held at the Bulawayo museum, pole-mounted at Thornhill in 1978, at the Zimbabwe Air Force museum at New Sarum 1983-1990, and at Gweru from 1993. The only Rhodesian Spitfire F.22 to survive; sister aircraft PK350 (SR64) was destroyed in a crash near Harare in 1982. Photographed in person on site by a visitor in July 2023, the most recent independent visual confirmation for any single Gweru airframe.

10813.description: Ex-Royal Rhodesian Air Force single-seat fighter-bomber. Compiler tables record the displayed marking and the true identity as the same, and the airframe is captioned simply as serial 112 in photographic records. One of three Vampires in the collection.

37951.description: c/n 7345101; ex-Aeroflot airframe retained at Massawa; logged 22 Dec 2014; may be a derelict rather than a display

10814.description: Ex-Rhodesian Air Force export-standard fighter-bomber, the second of the three Vampires held. Recorded in complete condition with the displayed marking matching the true identity.

10817.description: Ex-Rhodesian Air Force ground-attack Hunter of the type operated by No 1 Squadron. Complete airframe. Separately, one ex-Zimbabwean Hunter was gifted to the Chinese Aviation Museum in Beijing and is displayed there in British markings; that aircraft is not this one and is outside this region.

10818.description: Ex-Rhodesian Air Force piston basic trainer; T.52 was the export designation supplied to Southern Rhodesia. Complete airframe. Not the Provost gifted to the China Aviation Museum in Beijing: Oryx, 2 December 2022, lists a Canberra, a Hunter and a Provost as gifted to Beijing, while an Alamy photograph by Yagil Henkin taken November 2019 shows a Provost at Gweru. Two distinct airframes.

10816.description: Ex-Rhodesian Air Force Canberra light bomber, the type used by No 5 Squadron in the Bush War. Complete airframe. A second Zimbabwean Canberra, T.4 serial 2215, was recorded derelict at Manyame air base in 1996 and is not part of this collection.

10819.description: Ex-South African Air Force Harvard supplied to Southern Rhodesia in the early 1950s and serialled SR48. Complete airframe, photographed in the collection. Currency check September 2026: no post-2015 confirmation found; presence rests on undated compiler inventories and on photographs shot 2000-2006 but uploaded 2013-14, which read as recent and are not.

10821.description: Construction number 98. First flew at Hurn on 28 March 1956 and delivered to Central African Airways on 24 April 1956 as VP-YNA; leased to Air Malawi as 7Q-YDK from 1968 to 1979; returned as VP-YNA with Air Zimbabwe Rhodesia and then Air Zimbabwe; reregistered Z-YNA in October 1983 and withdrawn 31 May 1985 after 40580 flying hours. Handed to the museum in August 1986 and displayed at the entrance with the cockpit open to visitors. Confirmed in place by a dated photograph in November 2019.

10822.description: Homebuilt Mignet Pou du Ciel of the 1930s Flying Flea movement, held in the aviation collection with no serial or registration recorded by any inventory. Tandem-wing layout; classed here as a monoplane because each of its two lifting surfaces is a single wing rather than a stacked pair. Listed in complete condition. Currency check September 2026: no post-2015 confirmation found; presence rests on undated compiler inventories and on photographs shot 2000-2006 but uploaded 2013-14, which read as recent and are not.

10820.description: Ex-Southern Rhodesian Air Force elementary trainer, one of a batch delivered in the late 1940s and early 1950s. Two compilations give SR26 as both the displayed and the true identity; a third describes the aircraft as painted in the markings of the first Tiger Moth delivered to the SRAF, which leaves some doubt as to whether SR26 is the airframe or only the scheme. Identity retained here but treated as provisional. Currency check September 2026: no post-2015 confirmation found; presence rests on undated compiler inventories and on photographs shot 2000-2006 but uploaded 2013-14, which read as recent and are not.

10823.description: Cabin and fuselage shell only, construction number 4037, wearing the marking 6082. Photographed among the museum exhibits. Not carried by the aeroflight or Zimbabwe Field Guide inventories, which list eleven complete aircraft and omit it, so its identity as an exhibit rests on the photographic record and one directory listing. The marking 6082 is recorded as an alias rather than as the tail number because it has not been independently tied to this hull. Currency check September 2026: weak post-2015 support only. The Chronicle, 8 August 2022, lists an AB-205 among aircraft the facility houses, but the wording does not distinguish museum-held from Air Force of Zimbabwe airframes.

37961.description: c/n N.6474; plinthed at Meknes; logged 5 Sep 2018

37962.description: c/n N.6226; plinthed at Meknes; logged 9 Aug 2018

37963.description: Recorded as CNA-FE/05; c/n 1406029; a survivor of the small Soviet batch delivered to Morocco in 1961; logged 5 Sep 2018

37979.description: c/n PAC/56/389; gate guard at Moi Air Base Eastleigh; logged 21 Jul 2018

37980.description: c/n BH.120/388; displayed at Moi Forces Academy Lanet; first-hand sighting 23 Mar 2026

37982.description: Algerian Air Force MiG-17 recorded as 2523/275; displayed at the Musée central de l'Armée in the Riadh El Feth complex; logged 2 Apr 2016

37983.description: Royal Moroccan Air Force Mirage F1EH serial 167 downed over Western Sahara; the wreck is displayed as a war trophy by the Polisario Front at Rabuni; surveyed 19 Mar 2025

37985.description: c/n R.1190; displayed in the museum park; visit-dated Oct 2022; site record refreshed 19 Mar 2025

37986.description: Recorded as Y91602/AB; displayed in the museum park; visit-dated Oct 2022

37987.description: c/n 585812; displayed in the museum park; visit-dated Oct 2022

37992.description: c/n 20471; ex-Royal Air Maroc; preserved at the Casablanca-Anfa hangar; sighting refreshed Oct 2024

37993.description: c/n 21214; ex-Royal Air Maroc; sighting refreshed Oct 2024

37994.description: c/n 21216; ex-Royal Air Maroc; sighting refreshed Oct 2024

37995.description: c/n 749-2675; ex-Royal Air Maroc Constellation; a rare survivor; sighting refreshed Oct 2024

37996.description: c/n 1009; preserved with the Royal Air Maroc collection

10815.description: Two-seat Vampire trainer. The airframe wears the serial 4220 but its true identity is 2406; the aeroflight and Zimbabwe Field Guide inventories both carry an explicit displayed-identity versus real-identity distinction for this aircraft and the photographic caption record does the same. The false marking is recorded in aliases.

37563.description: c/n 071; ex-Alitalia Caravelle VI-N; the largest airframe on the beach; logged Nov 2018 and site record refreshed 22 Feb 2025

37564.description: c/n 17713; ex-Uganda government Boeing 707; the cockpit is open to visitors; logged Nov 2018

37565.description: c/n 34001212320; a Russian-registered Mi-26T retained at Aero Beach; a second entry lists it as removed from a neighbouring apron so its exact position has changed

37566.description: c/n 106; rear fuselage only; logged Nov 2018

37568.description: c/n 993428; Ugandan Air Force Delfin; the cockpit is open to visitors; logged Nov 2018

37569.description: c/n 96010001; the airframe is split into two parts; logged Nov 2018

37570.description: Ugandan Air Force MiG-21MF; the cockpit is open to visitors; logged Nov 2018

37571.description: c/n 27-2733; Ugandan Air Force Aztec; logged Nov 2018

9928.description: Boeing 737-277 Advanced, MSN 22650, built for Ansett as VH-CZR. Later N183AW with America West, then A6-AVA, UP-B3702 and YA-GAB with operators in the United Arab Emirates, Kazakhstan and Afghanistan, latterly ZS-BIL with Gryphon Airlines in South Africa. Moved from OR Tambo to Hoedspruit by road in May 2019 over nine days and across three provinces because a retired airliner cannot be flown into a bush estate. Now fitted out as six hotel cabins. Build date: the hotel's own account calls it a 39-year-old airframe in 2019, an aviation feature gives October 1981; 1981 used. The construction number 806 quoted in that feature is the Boeing line number, not the MSN.

9929.description: Boeing 727-191, built 2 June 1967 as N7273F for Frontier Airlines, later Braniff, then the Burlington Northern and Santa Fe Railway Company, then Dart and DSTS, and finally the Government of Djibouti as a presidential and VIP aircraft as J2-KBA until 2012. Stored at AeroNeXus at Johannesburg from September 2012 before moving to Hoedspruit, where it is fitted out as three VIP cabins. The hotel's own website calls it a Boeing 727-300, which is not a real variant; airhistory and airliners photo records confirm the 727-191. The construction number 418 quoted in an aviation feature is the line number and the MSN was not confirmed, so it is omitted.

9930.description: Gate guard at AFB Bloemspruit, home of 16 Squadron and 87 Helicopter Flying School. Listed in both the 2013 forum inventory and the current Unofficial SAAF Website list, and independently confirmed still on its pad on current Esri World Imagery: a small jet with an elevated shadow indicating plinth mounting, on the lawn of a walled compound beside the base HQ building. Satellite fix on the airframe: -29.103987, 26.310453.

9932.description: One of three ex-SAAF airframes displayed in the domestic area of AFB Langebaanweg, home of the Central Flying School. Three separate plinth-mounted airframes are visible on current Esri World Imagery around the main traffic circle, matching the three the SAAF list records here, but the imagery is only z18 and individual airframes could not be told apart, so no per-airframe coordinate is asserted. Marked FB.52 on the current SAAF list; the 2013 forum inventory called the same airframe a Vampire FB Mk 9. The discrepancy is unresolved.

37581.description: Same doubt as the 727 above; c/n 22650

9933.description: Ex-Central Flying School basic jet trainer displayed in the domestic area of AFB Langebaanweg. Present in both the 2013 forum gate-guard inventory and the current Unofficial SAAF Website list. One of three plinth-mounted airframes visible on current Esri imagery around the base traffic circle; individual identification from imagery was not possible.

9935.description: Ex-24 Squadron SAAF strike aircraft, mounted on a low plinth on open ground inside the base perimeter at the north-west corner of AFB Waterkloof, immediately behind the boundary fence on a public suburban street in Valhalla. Confirmed in position by a dated geotagged photograph of 24 May 2014 and again on current Esri World Imagery at z20. Satellite fix on the airframe: -25.816222, 28.210398. Remains SAAF property and is on the SAAF Museum inventory.

9936.description: Ex-12 Squadron SAAF dual-control trainer, on a plinth beside a public road inside the base's northern domestic area, about 560 m south of the Buccaneer. Confirmed by a dated geotagged photograph of 24 May 2014 and independently visible on current Esri World Imagery. Separate satellite fix on this airframe: -25.820901, 28.212164.

9937.description: Listed as an AFB Waterkloof static display on the Unofficial SAAF Website airframe list and named in a 2013 forum inventory. NOT found on satellite imagery in the northern base area or along the hangar line, and absent from the Wikipedia surviving-Sabres list, which records only 361, 367 and 372 in South Africa. Serial 369 is carried on the strength of the SAAF list alone; present location on the base and current condition unconfirmed.

37582.description: Licence-built Aermacchi MB-326M; the type the Central Flying School taught on until 2005; c/n A101

37587.description: Plinthed at AFB Waterkloof; c/n B3-12-63

37588.description: Plinthed 500 m from the Buccaneer; c/n HP-184B/71546

9934.description: Ex-SAAF advanced trainer displayed at AFB Langebaanweg. Present in both the 2013 forum inventory and the current SAAF list. The airframe mounted on a plinth in the centre of the base traffic circle on current Esri imagery has a single-engine planform consistent with a Harvard, which makes it the most likely of the three to be this aircraft, but the resolution does not settle it.

37600.description: c/n 19283; ex-Ethiopian Airlines DC-3; displayed at the Asmara Expo grounds; last positively logged 24 Oct 2014

37601.description: c/n 18255; ex-Kenyan operator; displayed at the Asmara Expo grounds; last positively logged 24 Oct 2014

37603.description: Plinthed at Bahir Dar; serial not recorded; logged 13 Mar 2018

37604.description: Plinthed at Bahir Dar; logged 13 Mar 2018

37605.description: Plinthed at Bahir Dar; logged 13 Mar 2018

9968.description: Former Silver Falcons aerobatic team aircraft, flown as Falcon 2 and Falcon 3. Pole-mounted in the grounds of Laerskool Impala since April 1998 and still wearing the orange white and blue Silver Falcons scheme. Confirmed in place by a dated photograph of 25 September 2022 carrying Silver Falcons and Central Flying School markings. Mounted close to the boundary and photographable from the street.

9974.description: Atlas Impala Mk I two-seat trainer on display at Queen's Fort. Serial 591 is given by the saairforce.co.za places directory and by aviationmuseum.eu's Queen's Fort page. A 2009 Impala survivors compilation instead lists 589 as a SAAF Museum aircraft on display and does not place 591 at Bloemfontein, so there is a 589/591 digit conflict that one telephone call to the museum would settle. A 2006 stock photograph confirms an Impala Mk I displayed at the fort.

9975.description: Atlas Impala Mk II on display at Queen's Fort. Serial 1032 is corroborated by two independent lineages: the aviationmuseum.eu and saairforce.co.za directory entries, and a 2009 Impala survivors compilation which records 1032 as SAAF Museum property on display at Fort Bloemfontein with build number 33.

9976.description: Dassault Mirage IIIRZ reconnaissance fighter, serial 837, at Queen's Fort. Only four RZs were delivered to the SAAF, numbers 835 to 838, so 837 is a plausible and scarce airframe. aviationmuseum.eu lists it as on display; the older saairforce.co.za directory described it as under restoration at the fort. Recorded as on_display with that earlier restoration note flagged.

9977.description: Listed at Air Force Headquarters, Pretoria in both the 2013 forum gate-guard inventory and the current Unofficial SAAF Website list. Current Esri World Imagery shows one plinth-mounted airframe with a swept planform at the south-west corner of the SAAF HQ block on Dequar Road, Salvokop. That sighting confirms at least one airframe is still standing, but the resolution does not distinguish a Mirage F1 from an Impala, and only one airframe was found where the list records two.

9978.description: Ex-Silver Falcons display-team aircraft, flown as team numbers 1, 3 and 4. Listed at Air Force Headquarters, Pretoria in both the 2013 forum inventory and the current SAAF list, and photographed there on 22 September 2018. A 2013 forum contributor recorded that it originally wore the orange white and blue Silver Falcons scheme but had by then been repainted all-silver, so its paint is not evidence of team identity. Only one airframe was found at the HQ site on current satellite imagery, so it is unresolved whether this Impala or Mirage F1CZ 202 is the survivor.

9981.description: Atlas Cheetah E, serial 826, displayed at the Sci-Bono Discovery Centre. 826 is confirmed by SAAF type documentation as one of the Mirage IIIEZ airframes converted to Cheetah E standard. Placement at Sci-Bono comes from aviationmuseum.eu's dedicated page for this airframe and independently from the saairforce.co.za places directory. DOUBT: neither source is recent and I found no dated photograph or visitor account from 2024-2026 confirming the aircraft is still on the site, so presence in 2026 is unverified.

38143.description: c/n 4340; preserved at Rabat-Sale; logged 17 Oct 2016

9983.description: Ex-SAAF interceptor displayed in the grounds of Sir Pierre van Ryneveld High School, Kempton Park, alongside a memorial to a former pupil killed flying a Bosbok during the Border War. Confirmed in place by dated photographs of 25 September 2022. Visible from Commissioner Street.

38180.description: One of two Canadian Super Constellations left at São Tomé after the 1968-70 Biafran airlift; c/n 1049H-4831

38181.description: Second Biafran airlift Super Constellation; c/n 1049H-4832

38182.description: Atlas rebuild of a Dassault Mirage IIIEZ; single-seat interim Cheetah E; c/n 450

14121.description: Construction number 9452. Esri WorldView-2 imagery of 3 June 2022 shows a complete, intact, all-white DC-3 standing alone on mown grass inside the N'Dolo perimeter, roughly 150 m clear of the general-aviation apron, with a footpath running to it and a low white structure alongside - a placed display rather than a parked or abandoned machine. A contributor notes the aircraft carries four-bladed propellers and doubts the engines are original R-1830s, which suggests the airframe has been cosmetically made up rather than left as retired. Caution on identity: the registration 9Q-CTR is also carried on the N'Djili boneyard listing by a dumped An-24RV, construction number 77310802, so the mark has been re-issued or mis-recorded somewhere on the Congolese register; the construction number is the firmer identifier here.

14122.description: Construction number 4831. Ferried to São Tomé on 30 July 1969 with CanRelief Air for the Biafran airlift and never left; with its sister CF-NAM it is the last physical remnant of the Biafra relief bridge. Retained beside the airport road and fitted out commercially, one airframe as a restaurant and the other as a discotheque. Currency is the weak point: the last first-hand account found is a Friends of São Tomé and Príncipe campaign report of 15 January 2020 describing both as standing but deteriorating and seeking monument status; OpenStreetMap carries a live restaurant node named The Airplane 25 m from the recorded position; but Esri WorldView-3 imagery of 17 September 2023 at this spot resolves only two long white fuselage-shaped objects among trees and buildings, with no wings distinguishable, and no complete four-engined airframe is visible anywhere else around the airport. Recorded as still present on the balance of that evidence, flagged as needing a ground check.

14123.description: Construction number 4832, the second of the pair ferried to São Tomé on 30 July 1969 for the Biafran airlift and left in place. Sources do not consistently say which of CF-NAL and CF-NAM became the restaurant and which the discotheque, so the fit-out is not attributed to either airframe individually. Same currency caveat as its sister: last confirmed standing by the January 2020 preservation campaign report, not unambiguously resolvable in the September 2023 satellite imagery.

14124.description: Chadian Air Force liaison aircraft, construction number 203M, coded preserved. The best-evidenced monument in this slice: Esri WorldView-2 imagery of 3 November 2021 shows a white aircraft of about 13 m span mounted on a circular grassed traffic island at a road junction inside the base, an unmistakable plinthed camp monument. Point-in-polygon testing against OpenStreetMap places the position inside the Chadian air force compound named Base ADJ KOSSEÏ, not the adjoining French camp.

38186.description: The third of the SAAF's eight Shackleton MR.3s; c/n 1533

14125.description: Gabonese Air Force liaison aircraft, construction number 101M, coded preserved within the military area on the seaward side of Libreville Léon-Mba. Not independently corroborated and not resolvable from satellite: the only Esri coverage of this block is 15 April 2017 at 0.5 m, at which scale a Broussard spans about eleven pixels. Recorded on the strength of the source's explicit preserved code and its specific construction number. Note the near-identical Chadian airframe TT-KAB, construction number 203M, also preserved - a French supply pattern to former AEF air arms, not a duplicate record.

14128.description: Congolese Air Force two-seat trainer, construction number 10994819 - a number in the Ulan-Ude plant 99 MiG-15UTI series, which supports the type attribution. Coded preserved and sited in the landscaped part of the military enclave on the west side of Pointe-Noire Agostinho-Neto, separate from the withdrawn MiG-21 line 350 m to the north. aviationsmilitaires.net describes the southern display aircraft as a MiG-17 rather than a MiG-15; that page gives no construction number and the disagreement is most likely a loose visual identification on its part, but it is unresolved. Esri imagery of 21 April 2021 for this block is capped at low zoom and shows an aircraft-shaped white object in the display area without allowing a type call.

14129.description: Congolese Air Force Noratlas, construction number 138, coded preserved and standing about 80 m south-south-east of the MiG. aviationsmilitaires.net independently records a Noratlas preserved in the southern part of Pointe-Noire air base, which corroborates presence and position though not the serial. The twin-boom planform of the white airframe visible in the 21 April 2021 Esri imagery at this position is consistent with a Noratlas.

14126.description: Gabonese Air Force Bandeirante, construction number 110360, coded preserved; the location entry was created on 20 May 2025 and carries a contributor comment quoting the registration and construction number together, which indicates a first-hand sighting rather than a copied listing. Single-sourced. Satellite confirmation not possible - the only Esri coverage here is from April 2017 and predates the report.

14131.description: Ex-Congolese airliner, construction number 19195. One of three airframes withdrawn at N'Djili, cut up, trucked east to the Nsele valley and reassembled on a landscaped hilltop in the park, where the three between them house a restaurant, a nightclub and a VIP lounge. spottingmode.com codes all three preserved. Esri WorldView-2 imagery of 3 June 2022 shows three complete airliners standing on made-up pads served by a loop access road, paved walkways and an adjacent building - a deliberate installation, not a dump. Which of the three carries which function is not separately sourced, so the fit-out is not attributed to individual airframes.

14132.description: Ex-Congolese airliner, construction number 20795. Second of the three airframes moved from N'Djili to the park and rebuilt on the hilltop display. Identified in the 2022 satellite image as the narrow-body with a conventional fin standing north-east of the TriStar.

14133.description: Construction number 1209, previously with Air Canada and Delta Air Lines, latterly Hewa Bora Airways. Stored at N'Djili from 2007, then cut into three sections, moved to the park and reassembled on the hilltop. Reported by aviation24.be in September 2019 as the centrepiece of a scheme to convert three aircraft into a bar-disco, a restaurant and a hotel. The largest airframe visible in the 2022 imagery, on a paved pad with an awning structure alongside.

14138.description: Single jet trainer on a tiered circular kerbed plinth in the centre of the Air Force Roundabout, on the public road outside the Air Force Military School Jos. Identified as NAF420 construction number 491015 by the Spottingmode location record at 9.87101N 8.88660E, seven metres from the plinth centre. Still in place in Google satellite imagery of 2026, where the planform measures roughly 11-12 m in both span and length, consistent with the L-29 at 10.29 m span and 10.81 m length and inconsistent with any larger twin; the wingtip tanks read as engine nacelles from directly overhead. NAF4xx is the Nigerian Air Force L-29 serial block - NAF409 construction number 993330 is a second preserved L-29 at Kano - while the L-39ZA block is NAF3xx. Serial and construction number rest on that single entry; no ground photograph was found.

14140.description: White high-wing twin standing alone on open ground beside an internal road at Base Aérienne 101 Niamey, about 200 m from the base mess. Construction number 4332. Recorded as preserved with a 22 December 2025 update; the airframe is unmistakable at the coordinate on Esri WorldView-3 0.31 m imagery acquired 29 January 2024.

14141.description: Armed trainer displayed at a road junction inside Base Aérienne 210, the Burkinabè air force's SF.260 home station at Bobo-Dioulasso. Construction number 343/29-037. Recorded as preserved from a first-hand visit dated 21 May 2025; a small aircraft-shaped object sits at the junction on Esri 0.34 m imagery acquired 28 October 2025. Variant unresolved: the source's construction-number-backed entry says WL while GlobalSecurity describes Burkina Faso's armed SF.260s as WP - four of which came direct from Italy and were stationed at Bobo-Dioulasso.

14148.description: Burkina Faso's only MiG-17F, a combat veteran of the 1985-86 Agacher Strip War against Mali, mounted on a landscaped and planted island inside the Ouagadougou air base. Recorded as preserved with a 22 December 2025 update, and a white swept-wing jet sits on the green island on Esri WorldView-3 0.31 m imagery acquired 10 December 2025.

10123.description: Ex-SAAF 35 Squadron, grounded 22 November 1977. Hoisted onto the roof of Vic's Viking Garage on 5 March 1987, replacing the Vickers Viking ZS-DKH that had stood there since January 1963. The garage passed to Sasol in 2004 and the aircraft has been repainted successively in SAAF, Coca-Cola and Sasol schemes; it is not in service colours. Still in place in Sasol livery in a dated photograph of 25 September 2022, photographed on the roof on 20 September 2018 with a coordinate fix on the airframe, and shown in place in a June 2024 blog post. Roof mounting, no access to the airframe itself, but fully visible from the R553.

10664.description: Ethiopian Airlines Dakota displayed landside on the Ring Road at the north-west corner of Bole International Airport. Painted as ET-T-1 which was the registration of Ethiopian Airlines' first DC-3 and is a commemorative marking rather than this airframe's identity; the true identity is ET-AIA. Photographed on display October 2019 and the location was refreshed by Spottingmode in July 2025.

10666.description: Former BOAC and British Airtours aircraft delivered as G-APFL, registered to Coastal Airways in 1981 but never operated. Airhistory caption of a March 2014 photograph describes it as preserved in the Aero Beach Club garden. The old British registration shows through the paint; the last legal identity was the Ugandan government one.

10668.description: Ex-Russian civil heavy-lift helicopter preserved in the Aero Beach grounds.

10669.description: Former Uganda Air Force basic trainer. Only the rear fuselage survives at Aero Beach.

10671.description: Uganda Air Force jet trainer preserved at Aero Beach. A second Ugandan L-29 U-107 is at Soroti and is not part of this site.

10677.description: Uganda Air Force fighter at Aero Beach now split into two sections. Identified from the construction number 10001 stamped in the wheel bay because no serial survives on the airframe.

10678.description: Uganda Air Force fighter at Aero Beach.

10682.description: Ethiopian Air Force gunship in the outdoor military hardware exhibition beside the Amhara martyrs' monument. No serial recorded so tail_number is blank. Visitor reviews from 2016 and 2019 describe old fighter planes and 1980s military hardware in the grounds.

10683.description: Ethiopian Air Force two-seat trainer in the outdoor exhibition at the Amhara martyrs' monument.

10684.description: Ethiopian Air Force strike aircraft in the outdoor exhibition at the Amhara martyrs' monument.

10685.description: Former Ethiopian Air Force 711, then an Ethiopian civil Dakota. Ruud Leeuw recorded it as a hulk near Asmara airport in 2003 and moved to the Expo Park in southern Asmara by June 2006. Its USAAF serial was 42-100820 which corresponds to the construction number 19283 that Spottingmode carries, so the two records agree.

10686.description: Kenyan-registered freighter damaged by a fuel truck in May 1998 and strafed by an Ethiopian MiG in June 1998 at Asmara. Stripped of engines and wings and moved to the Asmara Expo grounds in June 1999 where it serves as a children's playground.

10687.description: Soviet transport hit by EPLF rocket shrapnel and used as a barracks by Soviet advisers from 1986. Wings, stabiliser and tail section removed. Moved to the Asmara Expo grounds and used as a children's climbing frame.

10688.description: French Navy Skyraider preserved at the French air base at Djibouti and repainted in Armee de l'Air markings as 21-LP. Le Fana de l'Aviation reported the restoration. Last noted February 2025.

10689.description: Former Armee de l'Air Super Sabre preserved on the base wearing code 11-YB. Last noted February 2025. Two further F-100 airframes lie in a scrapyard at Balbala and are deliberately not recorded.

37826.description: c/n 182004804; ex-Kyrgyz operator; converted into the Guluf Airline Restaurant at Hargeisa; logged 18 Mar 2025

10690.description: Complete Mirage IIIC preserved on the base. Spottingmode carries the identity with an explicit caveat after a February 2025 contributor could not be certain which of the two Djibouti Mirage IIICs stands at this position; treat the serial as provisional.

10691.description: Second Djibouti Mirage IIIC surviving as nose section and fin only, a few metres from the preserved Skyraider. Last noted February 2025.

10700.description: Soviet transport preserved beside the Massawa to Asmara road at Massawa. Ruud Leeuw records an An-12 at the Massawa bus station and Spottingmode carries the identity with construction number 7345101. The most recent record found is from 2014 so continued presence is unconfirmed.

37837.description: c/n 168-377; displayed at Houmt Souk on Djerba; logged 11 Mar 2020 by observer R.H. Dijkhuizen

10701.description: Kenya Air Force piston trainer preserved on Moi Air Base at Eastleigh, away from the withdrawn DHC-5 Buffalo airframes elsewhere on the field. Last recorded 2018.

10702.description: Kenya Air Force Bulldog retired from service in November 2023 and gifted by the Kenya Air Force to Moi Forces Academy Lanet for its aviation technology programme. Handover reported by the Kenyan Ministry of Defence and DefenceWeb. A student started the engine at the handover ceremony so the airframe may retain some systems, but it is a permanent ground exhibit at the school. Position recorded on site in March 2026.

37840.description: Gate guard at Hurghada; sighting refreshed Jan 2024

10705.description: Ethiopian Air Force gunship captured by the TPLF and displayed in the open-air section of the Hawelti martyrs' memorial complex. Presence last independently recorded in 2015. The museum was looted during the Tigray war and an April 2024 visitor review confirms the site is open again but does not itemise the outdoor hardware. Currency check September 2026: no source dated 2021 or later shows or describes this airframe. The museum building was destroyed and looted during the 2020-2022 ENDF occupation of Mekelle (World Peace Foundation, photographs July-August 2022 and July 2023) and the site had reopened by April 2024, but no post-war source itemises the outdoor hardware. Presence unverified since 2015; no evidence of destruction either.

10706.description: Captured Ethiopian Air Force fighter in the open-air section of the Hawelti memorial. Presence last independently recorded in 2015. Currency check September 2026: no source dated 2021 or later shows or describes this airframe. The museum building was destroyed and looted during the 2020-2022 ENDF occupation of Mekelle (World Peace Foundation, photographs July-August 2022 and July 2023) and the site had reopened by April 2024, but no post-war source itemises the outdoor hardware. Presence unverified since 2015; no evidence of destruction either.

10707.description: Captured Ethiopian Air Force strike aircraft in the open-air section of the Hawelti memorial. No serial recorded so tail_number is blank. Dark-tourism.com describes this airframe as a MiG-27 which is a misidentification. Ethiopia never operated the MiG-27 and Spottingmode records the type as MiG-23BN. Currency check September 2026: no source dated 2021 or later shows or describes this airframe. The museum building was destroyed and looted during the 2020-2022 ENDF occupation of Mekelle (World Peace Foundation, photographs July-August 2022 and July 2023) and the site had reopened by April 2024, but no post-war source itemises the outdoor hardware. Presence unverified since 2015; no evidence of destruction either.

10708.description: Sudanese-registered light twin preserved in the Hawelti memorial grounds alongside the captured military hardware. An unusual inclusion whose provenance is not documented in any source found. Currency check September 2026: no source dated 2021 or later shows or describes this airframe. The museum building was destroyed and looted during the 2020-2022 ENDF occupation of Mekelle (World Peace Foundation, photographs July-August 2022 and July 2023) and the site had reopened by April 2024, but no post-war source itemises the outdoor hardware. Presence unverified since 2015; no evidence of destruction either.
